title: WebFlux multipart @RequestPart FilePart null for an empty file followed by other parts: raise the part reader buffering limits
errorSample:
java.lang.AssertionError: Response body expected:<received: test.txt> but was:<no file received>
    at org.springframework.test.util.AssertionErrors.fail(AssertionErrors.java:62)
    at org.springframework.test.util.AssertionErrors.assertEquals(AssertionErrors.java:129)
    at org.springframework.test.web.reactive.server.DefaultWebTestClient$DefaultBodySpec.lambda$isEqualTo$0(DefaultWebTestClient.java:585)
    at org.springframework.test.web.reactive.server.ExchangeResult.assertWithDiagnostics(ExchangeResult.java:231)
    at org.springframework.test.web.reactive.server.DefaultWebTestClient$DefaultBodySpec.isEqualTo(DefaultWebTestClient.java:584)
symptom: In a WebFlux controller the @RequestPart FilePart parameter is null (the app answers 'no file received') when a 0-byte file part is followed by other parts, while the same file as the last part is received.
cause: The default multipart reader keeps part headers and bodies in a size-limited buffer, and an empty part that is immediately followed by the next part's headers is lost when that buffering limit is reached.
fixSummary: Install a custom multipart reader with larger buffering limits in a WebFluxConfigurer: create a DefaultPartHttpMessageReader, call setMaxInMemorySize(...) and setMaxHeadersSize(...) with higher values, wrap it in MultipartHttpMessageReader and register it through configurer.defaultCodecs().multipartReader(...). With larger limits the empty file part is kept and delivered as a FilePart.
